reader.summary: The dominant story of the week was France and Germany sealing a landmark deal to slow Europe's shift to all-electric cars, effectively scrapping the 2035 climate-neutrality target for vehicles. The two countries agreed to allow the UK to join the EU car policy if it aligns on China tariffs, and the pact drew immediate reactions from motorists and industry. In parallel, the long-awaited Nord Stream sabotage trial opened in a German court, with a Ukrainian ex-officer facing a war-crime charge and the defense moving to dismiss the case. Germany also pushed the EU toward imposing caps on more Chinese imports, a hardening trade line that risks Beijing's ire. On the budget side, the finance minister announced a €50 million contribution to Ukraine and sought a debt-brake exemption to sustain that aid. UniCredit received ECB green light to take control of Commerzbank, a major banking reshuffle. Berlin planned to unveil an AI cooperation deal with Nvidia the following week and entered talks to buy a 50 percent stake in defense firm KNDS. Domestically, Chancellor Merz attacked political extremes while the AfD and BSW forged a pro-Russia, anti-Ukraine alliance, and Berlin's leftist parties moved a step closer to forming a government. Germany also slammed the US for pushing Russia's return to the G20.

key_events.event: France and Germany sealed a deal to scrap the 2035 all-electric mandate and slow the car industry's transition, with a conditional path for UK entry.
The Nord Stream pipeline sabotage trial opened in a German court, with a Ukrainian ex-officer charged with a war crime and the defense seeking dismissal.
Germany pushed the EU to impose caps on additional Chinese imports, a harder trade line that risks Beijing's reaction.
UniCredit received ECB approval to take control of Germany's Commerzbank, a major European banking consolidation.
Germany planned to unveil an AI cooperation agreement with Nvidia, as government sources confirmed the deal for the following week.
The German finance minister announced a €50 million contribution to Ukraine and sought a debt-brake exemption to sustain the aid.
Chancellor Merz vowed the government would fight on as the AfD and BSW forged a pro-Russia alliance calling for an end to Ukraine aid.
Germany entered talks to purchase a 50 percent stake in the defense firm KNDS.
Germany publicly warned against the US move to bring Russia back into the G20.

display.eli5:
Germany is juggling several big stories right now. The biggest is a court trial about who blew up the Nord Stream gas pipelines under the Baltic Sea in 2022. A former Ukrainian military officer sits in the dock, and his lawyers are arguing the whole case should be thrown out. Meanwhile, prosecutors want to show it was a deliberate act of war.

Also, France and Germany just made a huge deal to let gas-powered cars stick around longer instead of forcing everyone to go all-electric by 2035. Car companies, unions, and the UK are all scrambling to figure out what that means for jobs and factories. Expect a wave of reaction headlines from VW, BMW, and the works councils.

This week, Berlin is set to officially sign a big AI partnership with Nvidia, the chip company. That means new data centers and a government-backed cloud service. It was literally scheduled for next week, so it should show up as a single, concrete announcement.

Here's a surprise that could pop up: in Berlin, the left-wing parties (SPD, Die Linke, the Greens) have been fumbling around trying to form a city government for months. If they suddenly announce a name for their next mayor or a formal deal, that would be a real plot twist no one was expecting.
